correctness.summary: The comb is a proper locally finite R-tree. Its metric functionals are exactly the internals plus the unique-end Busemann function b=r-p. The endpoint formulas h_w(x_n)=n+L_n-2p(w) eventually and b(x_n)=L_n-n give the exact d-weak limit set. If L_n-n tends to -infinity, Busemann superlevel sets are bounded and compact-range d-weak nets converge metrically; otherwise a subsequence of endpoints has at least two distinct weak limits. The critical choice L_n=n makes the endpoint sequence converge to every point.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The inspected September 2026 Gutiérrez--Nevanlinna paper constructs the metric-functional weak topology and gives a snowflaked-line non-Hausdorff example, while the earlier paper gives bounded-sequence strong convergence in proper spaces and non-geodesic multiple-limit examples. Related CAT(0) work concerns different weak topologies. Targeted literature and current SCOPE searches did not locate a proper geodesic CAT(0) R-tree example with this d-weak topology, the exact endpoint limit-set formula, or the L_n-n Hausdorff phase transition. Residual risk remains because the motivating paper is extremely recent.

value.summary: The result shows that properness, local finiteness, geodesicity, and CAT(0) curvature do not repair the new metric-functional weak topology. It also gives a sharp geometric threshold on a natural one-ended comb family: the topology is metric exactly when the tooth-end Busemann heights tend to -infinity, and is non-Hausdorff otherwise; at the critical threshold it is T1 but hyperconnected.

limitations: The exact classification is restricted to the explicit one-ended comb family.
No classification of arbitrary or multi-ended R-trees is proved.
The result concerns the metric-functional d-weak topology rather than standard CAT(0) weak/Delta convergence or the co-convex topology.
The compact-range net lemma extends an existing bounded-sequence mechanism and is not claimed as a major independent contribution.
The motivating topology paper is extremely recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations remain a genuine originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
